pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As found by @liggitt, there is a bug in the EndpointSlice controller that can cause it to panic. This is caused by attempting to modify a Service object from an informer directly instead of first copying the object. This PR should fix that.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Unfortunately it turns out that one of my tests covering this was affected by this chance. There is both a fake clientset and fake lister that are initialized together but don't seem as connected as one would like - the test is adding the same resources to both the lister store and the fake clientset. The test that's affected relied on the client updating the EndpointSlice with the managed-by label followed by the lister listing EndpointSlices with that label. This previously worked since I was modifying the EndpointSlice in place. Now that I'm doing a proper deep copy here, that portion of the test is not effective. I've adjusted the test for now and added a TODO to fix the test. I'm assuming there's a better way to initialize a lister and fake clientset where I won't run into this kind of problem? The generation is here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpointslice/endpointslice_controller_test.go#L53. 

At this point, that specific function of that test is not particularly critical, and fixing this panic is, so I think it's worth moving forward with this fix as is unless there's something obvious I'm overlooking.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #85331

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
Fixes panic in EndpointSlice controller when setting managed-by annotation.
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:
- Enhancement Issue: kubernetes/enhancements#752

/sig network
/priority critical-urgent
/assign @liggitt

A simpler change would be to make the sync loop do just one thing per sync:

1. if the setup annotation/labeling is required, copy the service/endpoint objects before updating them, return `true, nil` from ensureSetupManagedByAnnotation, and return early from syncService, counting on the watch update event from the service annotation update to kick us again
2. split the two tests that are expecting both setup and sync actions into two tests each: one which checks setup actions, and one which checks sync actions
also opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85353 since the controller does not react to changes in endpointslice objects (like addition or removal of a managed-by label)

@liggitt that's a good idea, thanks! That's actually probably simpler than the implementation I just pushed up. The implementation I just added has the benefit of a single sync loop and only one added action (service patch), but it does spread out the code related to this further than it likely needs to be. I'll be offline for a bit, but will follow back up with this later this morning.

review_comments: I think you need to updatae testdata in `plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/bootstrappolicy/testdata/controller-roles.yaml`
This change seems separate from the panic fix though, maybe this should be in separatae PR or at least a separate commit?

Unfortunately these are both pretty tightly tied together. The reason this didn't surface before in tests is that it only occurs when EndpointSlice Controller is starting up with Services that have selectors that already exist in the cluster. Of course that's just about every cluster upgrade, but almost no commonly run e2e test seems to cover that, and sadly I missed that in my testing. 

If a Service does exist that would be managed by EndpointSlice controller, it attempts to add an annotation to that Service, and what @liggitt had found is that that code caused a panic. Fixing that panic brought me to issue 2 which was that I hadn't added Service "update" RBAC for the endpointslice controller. Without that, the first fix wasn't much good. So although they don't seem super related on the surface, they're both necessary. I don't mind splitting these into separate commits if that helps.
